ORDER 
1. This Application has been filed by the Resolution Professional (RP) 
under Section 33 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016  
(Code) for ini tiating the Liquidation Process of Marks Pryor 
Marking Technology Private Limited  (Corporate Debtor) based on 
the resolution passed by the Committee of Creditors (CoC). 
2. The facts leading to the filing of this Application are as follows: 
a. On a Petition filed by Shubham Electrotech Private Limited 
under Section 9 of the Code, the CIRP was initiated in respect 
of the Corporate Debtor and the Applicant was appointed  as 
the Interim Resolution Professional (IRP) of the Corporate 
Debtor. 
b. Pursuant to the appointment, the IRP caused a public 
announcement on 09.12.2023 in two newspapers, namely , 
‘Daily Financial Express’, Pune Edition (English) and ‘Dainik 
Loksatta’, Pune Edition (Marathi),  calling upon the claims 
against the Corporate Debtor on or before 20.12.2023. 
c. In response to the public announcement, the IRP received one 
claim by a Financial Creditor amounting to 
Rs.11,06,26,372.57/- and 10 claims by Operational 
Creditors, totalling Rs. 24,51,09,797/-.  Based on the claims 
received, the IRP constituted the CoC with the sole Financial 
Creditor, i.e., Bank of Maharashtra. 
d. As decided by the CoC at its 2 nd meeting, an ap plication for 
withdrawal of the CIRP was filed before the Adjudicating

Authority, which was disposed of with a direction to file an 
appropriate application under Section 12A of the Code along 
with Form FA.  Because the application for withdrawal was 
disposed of, the CoC decided to continue the CIRP. 
e. In the meantime, the statutory period of 180 days expired, 
and the Applicant filed an application seeking extension of the 
CIRP period, which was allowed by this Tribunal.  However, 
the CoC opined that there is less possibility of some interested 
party coming forward for placing a Resolution Plan since the 
Corporate Debtor had not been in operation for a long time 
and most of the assets of the Corporate Debtor have been 
realised by the Secure d Creditor under the SARFAESI Act 
before commencement of the CIRP. 
f. In the circumstances, the CoC has not approved any 
resolution for publication of Form G, appointment of valuers, 
appointment of transaction auditor, etc. Since the resolutions 
proposed by the Applicant were not considered by the CoC , 
the Applicant was left with no option but to put an agenda for 
liquidation of the Corporate Debtor.  Accordingly, the 7th CoC 
meeting held on 27.06.2025 , passed a resolution with 100% 
voting to com mence the liquidation process.  However, the 
CoC has not recommended any insolvency professional to be 
appointed as liquidator for the Corporate Debtor. 
3. We have heard the Ld. Counsel for the Applicant and perused the 
material available on record.

4. The recor ds reveal that this Application is filed for initiating 
liquidation of the Corporate Debtor based on the Resolution 
passed by the CoC.  The CoC formed this opinion without 
undertaking the publication of Form  G, valuation of assets,  
transaction audit, etc. , mainly because the Corporate Debtor's 
business was not operational . It is stated that the Co rporate 
Debtor generated no revenue and had no active contracts during 
the last four years. Further, the Corporate Debtor has no business 
assets of substantial value that could form the basis for revival or 
resolution. The Corporate Debtor possesses only one asset, i.e., a 
residential flat, which does not constitute a business asset, and 
the valuation available with the CoC is negligible compared to the 
outstanding balances. In light of this, the CoC, in its commercial 
wisdom, is not in favour of conducting the futile exercise of issuing 
Form G. 
5. The Applicant submits that he had conducted seven meetings of 
the CoC,  though no p rogress could be made in the CIRP.  The 
extended CIRP period also expired on 06.07.2024.  In the absence 
of any resolution plan for the Corporate Debtor and given that the 
CIRP period has expired , the Applicant is obligated to file the 
Application under Section 33(1)(a) of the Code.  Accordingly, the 
Applicant has filed this Application. 
6. It is observed that the CoC in its 7 th CoC meeting held on 
27.06.2025 passed the following resolution. 
"RESOLVED THAT  pursuant to the provi sions of Section 
33(2) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, the

7. As per Section 33 (2) of the Code, where the resolution 
professional, at any time during the corporate insolvency 
resolution process but before confirmation of the resolution plan, 
intimates the Adjudicating Authority of the decision of the 
committee of creditors approved by not less than sixty-six percent 
of the voting share to liquidate the corporate debtor, the 
Adjudicating Authority shall pass a liquidation order. A plain 
reading of this provision indicates that the decision regarding 
whether to liquidate the corporate debtor falls squarely within the 
commercial decision of the CoC. 
8. In the matter of Sreedhar Tripathy v. Gujarat State Financial 
Corporation and Ors. [(12.10.2022 - NCLAT): MANU/NL/0788/ 
2022], the Hon’ble NCLAT has stated in para 7 as under:  
“The Explanation under Section 33(2) has been inserted by Act of 
26 of 2019 contains the legislative declaration and intention. The 
CoC in the Legislative Scheme has been empowered to take decision 
to liquidate the Corporate Debtor, any time after its constitution and

       resolution process but before confirmation of                the resolution plan,
       intimates  the  Adjudicating  Authority  of  the  decision  of  the
       committee of creditors approved by not less than sixty-six percent
       of   the   voting   share   to   liquidate   the   corporate   debtor,   the
       Adjudicating  Authority  shall  pass  a  liquidation  order.  A  plain
       reading  of  this  provision  indicates  that  the  decision  regarding
       whether to liquidate the corporate debtor falls squarely within the
       commercial decision of the CoC.

8.     In  the  matter  of      Sreedhar  Tripathy  v.  Gujarat  State  Financial

       “The Explanation under Section 33(2) has been inserted by Act of

before confirmation of the resolution plan. The power given to the 
CoC to take decision for liquidation is very wide power which can 
be exercised immediately after constitution of the CoC. The reasons 
which has been given in Agenda Item 1, it is made clear by the CoC 
that the Corporate Debtor is not functioning for last 19 years and 
all machinery has become scrap, even the building is in dilapidated 
condition and the CIRP will involve huge costs. We are not convinced 
with the submission of l earned counsel for the Appellant that the 
CoC's decision is an arbitrary decision. CoC is empowered to take 
decision under the statutory scheme and when in the present case 
the decision of the CoC for liquidation has been approved by the 
Adjudicating Authority, we see not good ground to interfere at the 
instance of the Appellant. However, we make it clear that the 
decision taken by the CoC was in the facts of the present case and 
it cannot be said that whenever decision is taken for liquidation the 
same is not open to judicial review by the Adjudicating Authority 
and this Appellate Tribunal. It depends on the facts of each case as 
to whether the decision to liquidate the Corporate Debtor is in 
accordance with the I & B Code or not. With these observations, the 
Appeal is dismissed.”

have been carried out during the CIRP are still pending. These 
actions include taking custody and control of all assets of the 
Corporate Debtor, appointing registered valuers within the 
specified time to value the assets, and forming an opinion on 
whether the Corporate Debtor has been subjected to any 
transaction covered under Sections 43, 45, 50, and 66 of the Code. 
However, the Corporate Debtor ceased its business operations
